subject: unmowed lawn
title: What If You Never Mowed Your Lawn Again?

scenes.text: What if you never mowed your lawn again? Your yard would slowly try to become a forest.
Within weeks, dandelions and clover bloom. Lawns cut only every three weeks grow up to 2.5 times more flowers.
After one uncut May, British lawns held over 250 plant species between them, even wild orchids.
Around year five, brambles, shrubs and pine seedlings push up through the grass, if seeds blow in nearby.
After about 50 years, pines tower over the house. By year 100, oaks and hickories are catching up.
One English wheat field was abandoned in 1882. Half of it is woodland now. A lawn only exists because you mow.

description:
What if you never mowed your lawn again? A UMass Amherst study found lawns mowed every three weeks had up to 2.5 times more flowers, and Plantlife's No Mow May survey recorded over 250 plant species on unmown British lawns.
Left alone, open ground passes through grasses, shrubs and pines to hardwood forest over about a century; Rothamsted's Broadbalk Wilderness, abandoned in 1882, is now partly woodland.
